cards.text: Paul is writing to the churches of Galatia, and he's just told them to walk in step with the Spirit. Now he gets practical. If someone is caught in a trespass, he says, you who are spiritual have a job to do.

cards.question: Someone in the church is caught in a trespass. What does Paul tell the spiritual ones to do?
Paul says to restore the one caught in a trespass with a spirit of ___.

cards.text: Hold on, helper. Paul's got a word for YOU too: watch yourself.

cards.question: Paul tells the one restoring someone to watch himself. Why?

cards.text: Makes sense, friend. Reach too far into the back of a junk drawer to pull a buddy out, and now there's TWO of you back there. Then Paul tells everybody, 'Carry one another’s burdens.'

cards.question: When believers carry one another's burdens, Paul says they fulfill the law of ___.

cards.text: Next, Paul has a reality check for anybody feeling a little too big. He talks about someone who thinks he is something when he is nothing.

cards.question: Someone thinks he is something when he is nothing. Who does Paul say he's fooling?

cards.text: Friend, I KNOW this one: edges worn flat, still telling the rubber bands in that junk drawer I was the sharpest stamper in the kitchen. Paul's fix is simple: each one should test his own work.

cards.question: Paul says someone who tests his own work will have reason to boast in someone else.
Paul has already said to carry one another's burdens. Now what does he say each one should carry?

cards.text: Now Paul turns to anyone who receives instruction in the word. Somebody's been pouring the word into you? Paul's got something for you to do.

cards.question: Paul says the one being taught the word must share in all good things with someone. Who?

cards.text: Then Paul gets serious: 'Do not be deceived: God is not to be mocked.' And he pulls out a picture from the farm.

cards.question: Paul says, Whatever a man ___, he will reap in return.

cards.text: Paul says there are two ways to sow: to please your flesh, or to please the Spirit.

cards.question: What does Paul say the one who sows to please the Spirit will reap from the Spirit?
Paul says the one who sows to please his flesh will reap destruction from the flesh.

cards.text: Same with my oven: chocolate chip dough goes in, chocolate chip cookies come out, and the ONE time I yelled 'WHO PUT SPRINKLES IN HERE?' it was ME. Then Paul turns to the tired ones: 'Let us not grow weary in well-doing.'

cards.question: Paul says not to grow weary in well-doing, because in due time we will reap a ___.
Paul says we'll reap that harvest even if we give up.

cards.text: Paul's last line here: as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone. EVERYONE, friend, not just the people in your group chat.

cards.question: Paul says to do good to everyone, and especially to whom?

findings.problem: The card states facts from outside the passage: Paul writing to the churches of Galatia (Gal 1:2) and having just told them to walk in step with the Spirit (Gal 5:25). Neither carries its reference, and the card cites only Galatians 6:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Makes sense, friend.' / the junk drawer joke / 'Then Paul tells everybody...'. It is not the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke invents a past event from the junk drawer: Papa Dorin bragging to the rubber bands that he was the sharpest stamper in the kitchen. It also contradicts the backstory, which says that in the drawer he gave up on himself, didn't talk much and didn't joke at all. Jokes may only make up small moments around his bakery.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. It is the first card of stop 2, not the passage's opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup line 'he pulls out a picture from the farm' rules out the wrong answers 'says' and 'hides' on the next card's fill in the blank, which gives away 'sows'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Then Paul turns to the tired ones' names an audience the text doesn't give. Galatians 6:9 says 'Let us', addressed to all the readers, Paul included.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
